item.title: Nigeria, Russia move to ease trade, strengthen customs cooperation
item.description: By Providence Ayanfeoluwa The Nigeria Customs Service, NCS and Federal Customs Service of Russia have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening bilateral trade facilitation, intelligence sharing and customs enforcement, while exploring mutual recognition of their Authorised Economic Operator, AEO programmes. The service in a statement said the Agreement on Cooperation and Mutual Assistance in Customs Matters, CMAA provides a framework for collaboration in customs procedures, information exchange, financial integrity, border security and personnel capacity development. Speaking, Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, who led the Nigerian delegation, described the agreement as a strategic instrument for safeguarding economic integrity, securing supply chains and strengthening trade governance. He explained that the signing followed months of technical consultations, legal reviews and constructive engagements between both administrations. Adeniyi explained that the NCS had accelerated its digital transformation through the adoption of electronic systems for customs declarations, payments and submission of supporting documents. According to him, the reforms demonstrate that revenue generation and trade facilitation can complement each other, in line with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards. On the implementation of the agreement, the Customs boss identified cooperation between the two countries’ AEO programmes as a major priority. He said both administrations would exchange experiences on their respective frameworks and operational procedures, with the long-term objective of achieving mutual recognition to facilitate the movement of cargo and reward compliant traders. The two sides also explored arrangements for exchanging customs statistics and trade data to improve analysis of bilateral trade flows. Adeniyi disclosed that Nigeria was participating in the World Customs Organisation’s data initiative. Russia’s Head of Customs, Valery Pikalyov, explained that his administration was authorised to collect and exchange customs statistics derived from declarations. Pikalyov expressed readiness to explore a dedicated data-sharing arrangement with Nigeria. The agreement also provides for cooperation against customs offences, illicit financial flows, grey-market importations, tax evasion, counterfeit goods, narcotics and other prohibited or hazardous materials. It further establishes a framework for direct operational assistance, personnel training and the exchange of professional expertise between the two administrations. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. item.title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
item.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. item.title: ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process. Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday. He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980. The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole. “Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. “They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo. “I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives. “There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. “I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process. “Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.” The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved. “I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule. “The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government. “For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology. “People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government? “These were reasonable questions. I suspect some of them would have kept you awake at night. “But for Jim Nwobodo, the fact that a problem is difficult does not mean we can afford to avoid it. “In July 1980, Anambra State University of Technology was established. item.title: Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State. Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm. The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post. According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops. He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away. Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him. He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital. Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested. He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace. Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction. “We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said. He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected. “Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. Our lives and livelihoods must be protected,” Apahar added. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments on the incident were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. item.title: FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026. President Bola Tinubu stated this yesterday at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, themed, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination.” Tinubu said Nigeria was determined to move beyond exporting raw mineral resources, stressing the need for investment in processing and beneficiation to strengthen domestic industries. “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities,” he said. The President said the government was working to build integrated value chains that would enable Nigerian enterprises to participate more actively in the mining industry and expand domestic capabilities. He urged investors to bring technology, finance and commercial expertise, assuring them of efforts to strengthen regulatory certainty and institutional support for sustainable returns. Earlier, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the sector from N6 billion annually before the administration to N100 billion in 2026. “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just N6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from N6 billion to N38 billion by 2024. “By 2025, it had risen to N70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the N100 billion mark this year,” Alake said. He attributed the growth to reforms and efforts to sanitise mining operations, including the establishment of Mining Marshals, which he said had apprehended over 300 illegal operators and recovered more than 100 mining sites. Meanwhile, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said revenue generated by agencies under his ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025. He cited improvements in maritime security, port reforms and approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy, while urging investors to explore opportunities in shipping, ports, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture and logistics. item.title: Tinubu reiterates commitment to respecting court judgments
item.description: By Henry Ojelu President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to respecting court judgments. He also conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, GCON, Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN. President Tinubu at the launch of a six-volume book, Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, organised to celebrate the senior lawyer’s 75th birthday, 50 years at the Bar and 35 years as an SAN, said: “Our administration respects court judgments, even the ones we do not enjoy reading. We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary. A government that bullies its judges only weakens its own foundation. “This administration passed the Judicial Officeholder Salary and Allowances Act 2024, reversing over 15 years of stagnation and delivering a 300 percent increase in the salaries of our Judicial Officers of the Superior Court of record. “We are not yet at our desired designation. But significant work is in progress, and the brighter future is now in closer view. We will be there, my Lordship. Our administration respects court judgment, even the one we do not enjoy reading. “We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary,” President Tinubu reassured. Tinubu urged stakeholders in the justice sector to promote Nigeria as a business-friendly destination, stressing that timely judgments could strengthen investor confidence. “Every timely judgment is an advertisement for the Nigerian economy,” he said. He congratulated Olanipekun on his professional milestones, noting that the senior lawyer had positively impacted Nigeria and humanity through his legal practice and mentorship. Tinubu described Olanipekun as a phenomenal Nigerian and outstanding advocate who had upheld the traditions of excellence in the legal profession. The President also acknowledged the lawyer’s decades of loyalty and friendship, disclosing that Olanipekun had led his legal team for decades. “On a personal note, I celebrate decades of loyalty, friendship, commitment and reciprocity between Wole Olanipekun and I. He has led my legal team for decades. In politics, friends come and go. Wole came, and Wole stayed,” he said. Tinubu said Olanipekun also led the legal teams that defended three of his predecessors when their election victories were challenged. He said the senior lawyer had consequently served as lead counsel to four successive Nigerian presidents since 2007, describing the record as unprecedented. “Presidents change. Parties change. The Lead Counsel remains,” he said. President of the Senate Godswill Akpabio lauded President Tinubu for his commitment to justice, democracy, and national development. He assured the President that the National Assembly will continue to support all legal instruments that will promote justice, democracy and the rule of law. item.title: Dangote cement records 60% reduction in road traffic accidents
item.description: Dangote Cement Plc. has recorded a remarkable 60 per cent reduction in road traffic accidents, following the implementation of a comprehensive driver safety programme, underscoring the company’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and promoting road safety across its transportation operations. The milestone was announced at the 2026 Customer Truck Scheme, CTS, Annual Driver Safety Award and Recognition Programme, where the company celebrated drivers who demonstrated exemplary safety performance and maintained accident-free records throughout the assessment period. The achievement builds on an earlier 30 percent reduction in road traffic accidents recorded in 2023, following the introduction of the company’s Safety Improvement Plan. As part of the initiative, approximately 3,000 drivers were trained in defensive driving techniques and safe road-use practices. According to the company, the sustained decline in accidents reflects the effectiveness of continuous driver training, behavioural monitoring, corrective interventions, and the deliberate recognition of safe driving practices. Speaking at the event on behalf of the Group Sales and Marketing Director, the National Sales Director of Dangote Cement Plc, Mr. Dolapo Ali, noted that the rapid expansion of the company’s transportation operations had made road safety a critical business priority. He disclosed that the CTS fleet had grown significantly from 469 trucks in 2017 to over 2,500 trucks today, increasing the need for a more structured and proactive safety management approach. “Our business has experienced tremendous growth over the years, and with that growth comes greater responsibility. As the number of trucks and drivers operating across our roads increases, so too does our exposure to road safety risks. Protecting lives and ensuring safe operations must therefore remain at the heart of our transport strategy,” he stated. Ali explained that road traffic accidents peaked in 2021 and 2022, prompting the company to introduce its Safety Improvement Plan in early 2023. A key component of the programme was an intensive defensive-driving training initiative through which approximately 3,000 drivers received professional safety training. The intervention delivered immediate results, with accident rates declining by 30 per cent in 2023 compared to the previous year, followed by a further 60 per cent reduction thereafter. To strengthen compliance and encourage safer driving behaviour, Dangote Cement also deployed advanced telematics technology across its fleet operations. The system enables real-time monitoring of critical driving behaviours, including overspeeding, harsh braking, and aggressive acceleration. item.title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe & Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency. Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday. Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday. Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October. The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026. Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves. He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market. “With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said. Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows. Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply. “The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said. Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency. He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows. item.title: ‘He was a go-getter’ – Taiwo Obe, Providus Bank mourn Ajasa
item.description: THE Chairman and founder of Journalism Clinic, Mr Taiwo Obe, has described the late Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers, Mr Femi Ajasa, as a go-getter, regretting that his death has robbed journalism of one of its brightest young professionals. Similarly, Providus Bank, one of Nigeria’s new-generation banks, has expressed sadness over Ajasa’s demise, saying his death is a loss not only to Vanguard but also to the media industry. In a condolence letter by its Group Head, Brand and Corporate Communication, Dafe Ivwurie, the bank said: “We were deeply saddened to learn of the death of Olufemi Ajasa. “By all accounts, he was an accomplished and highly respected digital journalist whose professionalism, dedication, and commitment to excellence contributed immensely to the growth and reputation of Vanguard’s digital media platforms. His passing at such a young age is a great loss not only to Vanguard but also to the Nigerian media industry.” Meanwhile, Obe, who took to his Facebook page to mourn Ajasa, described him as one of the first journalists trained at his clinic. He recounted the events that brought him close to the deceased and traced the history of their relationship until Ajasa’s death on Sunday. Obe said: “Circa 1997, TaijoWonukabe Limited, which I co-founded about two years earlier, moved from its garage office graciously donated to us by the prolific columnist, late Pini Jason Onyegbadue, into a three-bedroom bungalow on Bassie Ogamba Street, off Adeniran Ogunsanya, in Surulere, Lagos. “That property belonged to Madam Pemu, a relation of Sam Amuka-Pemu, the legendary journalist, Uncle Sam. “One day, not long after we moved in, Uncle Sam showed up, to greet Madam Pemu, who lived in a separate bungalow on the same premises. “I knew him then more by name than physical interactions. Either when he was leaving or as he alighted, I approached him, to introduce myself and after we exchanged pleasantries, he said: Money is good. See how you boys have changed this building. “From that day till date, we became connected. Fast forward to circa 2015: I had founded The Journalism Clinic and converted and renamed the hall which was the finishing room of PrintPro Projects Limited – the printing subsidiary of TaijoWonukabe – to The Hub – the training room of The Journalism Clinic at Anifowose, around the corner from Bassie Ogamba. “Uncle Sam visited one afternoon and declared ‘Vanguard will send people to all the training you will do here’.” He kept his word and the first paid training we had in The Hub included three participants from Vanguard Online Desk and Olufemi Ajasa was one of them. “A fine gentleman, two days ago, Vanguard reported his passing after a brief illness. Since that training, I had encountered Femi in various places and positions. He remained as respectful as ever; always go-getting and consistently impeccably-dressed. This really hit hard. item.title: Tinubu moves to achieve 40% fares reduction under NACTP
item.description: President Bola Tinubu in his determination to achieve the 40 percent fare-reduction target under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria. This followed his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country. Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, in a statement, yesterday, noted that the investment would support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, NACTP, in collaboration with state governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 percent on participating routes, in line with the President’s renewed hope agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031. Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Pi-CNG & EV, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026. Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers. Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries. The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, MDGIF, and private sector investors. These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses. President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments. The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings. He stresses that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs. item.title: Failure of privatisation in the electricity sector, by Adekunle Adekoya
item.description: FOR many reasons, Nigeria will continue to befuddle rational minds because things that work easily in other climes don’t seem to work here, whereas other things deemed impossible elsewhere work effortlessly here. The telecommunications sector is one example. There was no chance for the sector, given the status of the electricity sector. When GSM came in 2001, a major concern was how to power the base stations that would distribute the signals. Of course, the only viable option was to go the way of using generators. More than 25 years after, there are about 137,992 base transceiver stations, which has helped move teledensity from a mere 400,000 lines to more than 140 million lines as we speak. Of course, none of the telcos are owned by any government. The telecoms sector is thundering along, delivering value to investors largely on generated power. One of the cardinal reasons often advanced to justify the need for privatisation of state-owned enterprises is that efficiency and service delivery will improve. This raison d’être failed completely in the Nigerian case, especially the electricity sector. The privatisation effort first saw the creation of PHCN from NEPA, and then, unbundling into the Transmission Company of Nigeria, the generating companies, GENCOs, and the distribution companies, the DISCOs. That, as I see it, is where privatisation ended. In terms of service delivery, I am of the bent that the personnel of many of the DISCOs still carry on like employees of the civil service, or other government parastatals. Response to issues in the distribution chain, like a faulty transformer, or feeder pillar, are so slow that you wonder what work they do in their offices. In other countries where outages occur, power is switched from another station to serve the area without power until issues are resolved. Here we don’t have that luxury; there is not enough to go round in the first place, so you can’t switch to support those with outages. Apart from that, the way our towns and cities are wired leaves you wondering about the state of mind of those who did the wiring. This is obvious when there is an outage, and you discover that the house opposite you and that beside you still have light. How? One emergent trait of DISCO officials is to seek to make money from the distress of fellow citizens. If your transformer gets faulty, residents will be faced with a plethora of demands that they will have to contribute to fund, because they don’t “have the materials in store.” I was talking about tardy response. This is distressing because the shortest time people get a faulty transformer replaced is anything from a month to six months or one year. Areas without “influential” residents have been without light for more than three years as a result of a faulty transformer. item.title: Positioning Nigerian oil sector amid Mid-East ruptures
item.description: The Federal Government’s announcement of $21 billion in prospective foreign investment commitments for Nigeria’s oil and gas industry presents an opportunity the country must not squander. Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Heineken Lokpobiri, disclosed the development on 9th November, 2026, following engagements at the Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC). ADIPEC, an annual event held from 2nd to 5th November, is a major global energy exhibition and conference bringing governments, oil companies, investors, financiers and technology providers together to discuss energy security, innovation and investment opportunities. Its 2026 edition attracted about 240,000 participants from 170 countries and recorded thousands of agreements valued at $67 billion. Nigeria’s $21 billion comprises two non-binding memoranda of understanding: one investor group indicated willingness to mobilise $15 billion, another $6 billion. Their identities, nationalities and proposed Nigerian partners remain undisclosed. Neither the projects nor the division between exploration, production, gas and infrastructure has been specified. These are expressions of interest, not funds received or projects at final investment decision. The Government must turn them into bankable agreements. The attraction is understandable. Middle Eastern wars, rivalries and threats around the Strait of Hormuz, Suez Canal and Bab el Mandeb Strait expose global supply to geopolitical coercion. In 2025, about 20 million barrels of oil daily, roughly a fifth of global petroleum liquids consumption, passed through the Hormuz chokepoint. Disruption can raise shipping, insurance and energy costs worldwide. Investors therefore need geographically diversified production. Nigeria offers an Atlantic-facing alternative, away from the Gulf’s immediate flashpoints. Our attractions are substantial: 37.01 billion barrels of oil and condensate and 215.19 trillion cubic feet of gas, according to NUPRC’s January 2026 reserves estimate. Yet October crude production averaged only 1.51 million barrels daily, excluding condensates. The 2026 licensing round, offering 40 blocks, is another opportunity to attract exploration capital. But investors will not overlook oil theft, pipeline vandalism, insecurity, community disputes, spills, gas flaring, opaque contracts, corruption, multiple taxation, costly logistics and regulatory delays. The Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) must be implemented consistently, while fiscal terms, royalties, host-community obligations and contracting procedures are periodically reviewed. Reforms must offer predictability without surrendering Nigeria’s fair share. The government should disclose the investors when commercially permissible, publish project milestones, insist on beneficial-ownership transparency and report actual disbursements, jobs and production additions. item.title: The Big Three in Yalta-like summit to calm unsettled waters, by Owei Lakemfa
item.description: The United States, US President Donald Trump touched down in Shenzhen, Southern China, like a rain-soaked chicken. His wings had this month been clipped by massive Democrat victories in the midterm elections. Not his usual swagger, as if he owns the world. He travelled for a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Trump had eliminated the Iranian leadership but failed to conquer the Iranians who today hold firm to the Strait of Hormuz, giving passage to only ships they grant permission. Nine ships which, a few weeks ago, tried to circumvent the Iranians were disabled. The attacks on Iran had increased the global cost of oil and energy. Trump had also abducted a sitting President, Nicholas Maduro, and his wife right inside their bedroom in Caracas and introduced chaos in world markets with tariffs that can best be described as insane. Generally, he has made the world unsafe. Now, he was in China to see how a world he has contributed to set adrift can be anchored. The excitable Trump seemed wowed by the reception he received when he touched down: “This is a great president, one of the great presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody… And not only that, the fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people, the young children, the soldiers, the whole thing.” Trump said he and the Chinese and Russian leaders are uniquely positioned to reduce the world’s nuclear weapons stockpile and lessen the risks that they will ever be used. He said that the power of having such weapons can be intoxicating, which is why the US wants to deny Iran the ability to produce them. In 2026 estimates, the USA and Russia hold about 8,000 nuclear warheads, and China, 600. Trump also condemned “rogue globalist organizations.” He named the International Criminal Court as one of those and also referred to the Russo-Ukrainian War. He said the trilateral was history-making, adding: “Too often past leaders have avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements…We feel the opposite.” Host Jinping maintained his generally dignified composure. He did not react to claims by Japan and Taiwan about alleged Chinese and Russian aggression. He simply told Trump to “do the right thing” about Taiwan, over which China has historical claims. Jinping agreed that nuclear weapons should be comprehensively prohibited and destroyed, warning that there can be no victory in a nuclear war. When major powers clash, the world falls into turmoil.” On conflicts around the world, the Chinese President said: “China, Russia, and the United States should continue encouraging parties to conflicts to sit down and engage in talks, and resolve disputes through political and diplomatic means.” Just before the trilateral, the US had imposed further restrictions on Ch

item.title: From political patronage to institutionalised community prosperity: A new social contract for Nigeria
item.description: BY VICTOR-BANDELE DADA What happens to a community’s prosperity when the political leader who represented it leaves office? Does its fortune decline with the departure of its benefactor, or does it possess institutions that sustain it regardless of who holds power? The question exposes a structural weakness in Nigeria’s development experience: community advancement depends too heavily on the goodwill, generosity and discretion of individual officeholders. In my earlier Vanguard article, Reconciling Political Leadership with Community Prosperity, I argued for a constructive relationship between political leadership and economically empowered communities. Here I take the argument further. Nigeria must move from a culture of patronage to a culture of institutions. The limits of patronage Elected representatives are routinely approached for school fees, medical bills, jobs and business capital. These requests arise from real hardship, and responding with compassion is commendable. The difficulty is not generosity. It is that personal assistance, however well meant, cannot substitute for sustainable economic organisation. No governor can finance the aspirations of every citizen. No legislator can employ every constituent. No local government chairman can meet every household’s needs indefinitely. When expectations gather around individuals, development shrinks to what officeholders can personally distribute, and citizens become petitioners rather than participants in wealth creation. This burdens leaders unfairly and leaves communities exposed whenever administrations change. Redefining the purpose of leadership Government must keep discharging its core responsibilities: security, justice, education, healthcare, infrastructure and sound regulation. Community self-organisation can never excuse the state from these duties. But government can also facilitate institutions through which citizens organise their productive capabilities, mobilise resources and build enterprises. Compare financing one person’s immediate need with enabling an institution that sustains employment for hundreds. The first offers relief; the second builds lasting capacity. This is the transition Nigeria needs: from distributing the benefits of political access to institutionalising the opportunities of economic participation. The institutional pathway Prosperity Governance and Management (PGM) offers an integrated approach, organising human knowledge, occupational capabilities, productive resources, economic institutions and governance arrangements. Central to it is Community Insulation from Political Corruption: institutional arrangements that protect community economic institutions from partisan interference and the personal discretion of officeholders. This is not insulation from government. It is a framework for partnership with responsible political leadership on transparent terms. item.title: Obalende MTN bus park to open December, accommodate 1,000 buses — Wahab
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has said the ongoing redevelopment of the Obalende Bus Park, known as the Y’ello Bus Park, will be completed and ready for public use by the end of December 2026. The facility, being developed by MTN Nigeria as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, is designed to accommodate more than 1,000 buses. Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed this during an inspection tour of the Obalende project and another MTN-sponsored under-bridge recreational park at Falomo, Ikoyi. Wahab, who was accompanied by key government officials, including the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, Sola Giwa; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Adekunle Akodu; General Manager of the Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency (LASPARK), Adetoun Popoola; and Director of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, said the six-week completion window was agreed upon after consultations with stakeholders to resolve operational challenges. He explained that the project was initially scheduled for completion within 21 weeks following an inspection of the area by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and his deputy as part of efforts to transform the previously degraded environment into a modern transport hub. However, construction was delayed by logistical challenges involving existing transport operators conducting business at the site. Wahab said the government had engaged the transport unions, contractors and the Special Adviser on Transportation to agree on temporarily relocating operators from the immediate construction area to enable the contractors to complete the work. “Today was just to see how far they’ve gone. Thankfully, they had one or two logistics issues that had to do with the businesses that have been operating there, legacy things like the transport business. “We had to engage the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, the transport unions, and the contractors to see how we can give them a space for a maximum of six weeks—not shutting the place down 100 per cent, but moving them out of that immediate workspace to enable the contractors to complete it and hand it over to them to operate,” he said. The upgraded facility is designed to accommodate approximately 1,000 buses and will feature dedicated parking and loading bays, sleeping facilities for drivers, modern toilet facilities and green areas. The design also incorporates collapsible barriers along the perimeter to allow drainage maintenance teams access to the adjoining canal for regular cleaning and maintenance. Addressing concerns about possible commercialisation of the facility and increases in transport fares, Giwa assured commuters and commercial transport operators that access to the terminal would be free. “No, there’s no toll at all. item.title: ‘Obi Will Disgrace Him Spectacularly In Anambra,’ Momodu Dismisses Soludo’s Victory Promise For Tinubu
item.description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, has dismissed Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s prediction that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that Peter Obi will defeat the President in the state. Momodu, the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, said Obi would defeat Soludo “spectacularly” during the election. “With due respect to Prof. (Soludo), he has joined those people I said were speaking like robots about Tinubu. “I guarantee you that Peter Obi will disgrace him spectacularly during the election,” he said. The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Asked whether Obi could win Anambra despite Soludo and former governor Chris Ngige supporting Tinubu, and whether he had seen the crowd at the APC rally in the state, Momodu dismissed the significance of the gathering. “It’s good to see the crowd, but I am telling you they are beginning to nauseate Nigerians, and that is why Nigerians are shouting ‘bamayi, bamayi’,” he said. He also claimed that criticism of Tinubu was growing, with leaders increasingly expressing their dissatisfaction with the president. On the APC’s campaign activities across the country, Momodu argued that the ruling party’s extensive mobilisation reflected its concerns about the outcome of the election. “The only reason they are going everywhere feverishly is because they know they will lose the election. I am 66-plus. I have never seen this kind of campaign where the President is beginning to sound like an opposition leader,” he said. Momodu also accused Tinubu of treating APC governors like “robots,” alleging that their public statements appeared coordinated. “I monitored each of the governors. Let me tell you emphatically that they are being treated like robots. There is no question about it,” he said. ﻿ Soludo had earlier on Thursday declared that Tinubu did not need to rig the 2027 election because his administration’s performance would secure his re-election. “To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others,” he said at an APC presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by top party chieftains. item.title: 2027: People Are Rejecting Tinubu, They Can Feel The Pain — Dele Momodu
item.description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, says Nigerians are rejecting President Bola Tinubu because they are feeling the adverse impact of his administration’s economic policies. Momodu, who is the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presidential campaign council, said the growing public discontent was a reflection of the hardship Nigerians have endured since the removal of the fuel subsidy. The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. A combo of Dele Momodu and President Bola Tinubu Momodu said the government should have carefully considered the advantages and disadvantages of the policy before implementing it. He likened the country’s economic situation to a patient who had been given an injection and remained in a coma for almost four years. “That’s what is happening in Nigeria. And that is why you can see that everywhere Tinubu goes now, he is being rejected by the people. The people are not stupid; they are rejecting him because they can feel the pain,” he said. ﻿ The publisher accused the President of insensitivity to Nigerians’ economic hardship, citing excessive government spending, inadequate funding of critical sectors and the burden of subsidy removal. “We’ve since discovered that this subsidy issue could have been better handled because, if you look at it, the people who are at fault are probably less than 1,000 people, and now you are punishing over 200 million Nigerians because of the sins of a few people. “If he were sharing in the pain of the people, he would not be doing what he is doing, donating one billion, doing a budget to individuals, a budget in trillions, more than what you are paying the military, more than what you are using to service the health sector, more than what you are spending on the education of our children,” Momodu said. Momodu accused the Tinubu administration of covertly reinstating fuel subsidies and dismissed positive economic assessments by the World Bank and IMF, arguing that they had not improved Nigerians’ living conditions. “The world is praising us; the World Bank is praising us; the IMF is saying we are doing well. Whenever the IMF or World Bank is interested in your case, then something is wrong. You can see clearly that everything you can say is not affecting our people positively. Nigerians are suffering, and that’s just the truth,” he said. Since that announcement, the policy, alongside the unification of the foreign exchange market, has contributed to higher petrol prices and increased living costs for Nigerians. item.title: Yiaga Africa Urges INEC To Publish Guidelines For Nov. 28 Mock Accreditation
item.description: Yiaga Africa has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish comprehensive guidelines and the list of participating polling units for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic results upload exercise scheduled for November 28. The organisation said timely access to information about the exercise was necessary to enable citizens, political parties, civil society organisations, election observers, and the media to understand, participate in, and monitor the process. In a statement signed by its Executive Director, Samson Itodo, Yiaga Africa welcomed INEC’s decision to conduct the exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections. It said the exercise was consistent with sustained calls by citizens and civil society organisations for the commission to adequately test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) before the elections. COMBO: Photo of YIAGA Africa executive director Samson Itodo and INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan “However, Yiaga Africa is concerned that, despite the importance of the exercise, the Commission is yet to make public comprehensive guidelines and a framework outlining how it will be conducted. The list of polling units where the exercise will take place is also yet to be made public. “For an exercise of this significance, timely access to information is essential. Citizens and electoral stakeholders should have sufficient information and notice to understand, participate in, and observe the process,” the statement read in part. Yiaga Africa said transparency in the exercise would be crucial to building public confidence in the electoral technologies that would be deployed for the 2027 elections. It called on INEC to immediately publish a comprehensive framework outlining the scope, modalities and procedures for the exercise. The organisation also urged the commission to release the complete list of participating polling units and other relevant locations early enough to give stakeholders sufficient time to prepare for the exercise. Yiaga Africa further urged INEC to use the mock exercise as an opportunity to demonstrate transparency and responsiveness while allowing meaningful public scrutiny of BVAS and IReV. Last week, INEC had announced November 28 as the date for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise to test its voter accreditation and electronic results transmission systems ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission’s chairman, Joash Amupitan, said the exercise would simulate the presidential election and take place across all states of the federation. He said the exercise was part of measures to address technical challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections and strengthen the credibility of the 2027 polls. The 2027 Presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will be held on February 6. item.title: Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report
item.description: Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group. The fifth edition of the State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, published on Thursday, highlighted the rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructure across the continent but warns that access alone has not translated into widespread everyday usage. According to the report, 89 per cent of African adults live in countries with access to an instant payment system. However, a survey of 1,403 digital payment users across 15 markets found that 55 per cent still use cash for about half of their transactions. It also found that more than half of respondents had experienced payment problems, including delays and transfers to the wrong recipients, while one in three affected users never reported such incidents, largely because they did not know how to do so. “Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems; today there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system IIPS,” said Sabine F. Mensah, who is Deputy CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation and lead author of the report. “The question has changed. It is no longer whether Africans can pay instantly, but whether they trust the system enough to stop reaching for cash. Our research shows that trust is won in seconds, through a payment that goes through instantly, with preventive safeguards such as recipient name validation, and a payment confirmation message received in real time. It is kept by getting timely resolution and people’s money back when something goes wrong.” (L-R): Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Sabine Mensah; CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Robert Ochola; and Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Akinwale Goodluck, at the report launch on Thursday, November 19, 2026. 39 Instant Payment Systems The report identified 39 live instant payment systems across Africa, comprising 35 domestic systems in 29 countries and four regional systems. Overall, 43 African countries now have access to instant payment capabilities through domestic or regional platforms. Four domestic systems were introduced in the past year in Liberia, Burundi, Guinea and Mauritania, while a new regional system now serves the eight countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). Another 17 countries have instant payment system projects underway. Transaction volumes, according to the report, have grown by an average of 28 per cent annually since 2021, while the average transaction value has declined from $45 to $26, indicating increased use for smaller, everyday purchases.
